discovery: Discovery of the high-confinement (H-mode) regime in magnetically confined plasmas and its explanation by sheared-flow suppression of turbulence

nominees.name: Fritz Wagner
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics, Greifswald, Germany

nominees.name: Patrick H. Diamond
nominees.affiliation: University of California San Diego, USA

motivation: In 1982 Fritz Wagner and colleagues at ASDEX found that a tokamak plasma, once heated beyond a threshold, spontaneously changes to a state where energy confinement roughly doubles and a steep edge transport barrier forms. This H-mode showed that turbulent plasmas can organise themselves into states of better confinement. Patrick Diamond developed the theory showing that sheared E×B flows decorrelate turbulent eddies and that turbulence-driven zonal flows regulate transport. Keith Burrell's measurements on DIII-D confirmed this mechanism directly. Together these results give a clear physical account of how nonlinear physics creates transport barriers. That account is now used well beyond fusion, in geophysical and astrophysical flows. The H-mode is also the baseline operating regime for ITER and for reactor designs. Few discoveries in plasma physics have done as much to turn fusion energy from a hope into an engineering programme.
